Mr.Anand Bhatt, learned counsel for respondents No.1 an  Mr.Amol Shrivastava, learned counsel for respondent No.
 ORDER

The petitioner has filed this contempt petition alleging non-compliance of the order dated 08.01.2024 passed in W.P. No.31384/ 2023.
2.
By the said order, the Writ Court directed that a final order be passed in the matter within a period of two months from the date of receipt of information.

3. The respondents have fired their reply, stating that the Land Acquisition Officer has passed a final order in which it was observed that the process of declaring Gandi Basti under the Madhya Pradesh Gandi Basti Samunnity (Bhu- Arjan) Adhiniyam, 1956 was initiated.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Gandi Basti Samunnity (Bhu- Arjan) Adhiniyam, 1956
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. A notification for such declaration was published in the Gazette dated 25.05.1973, and an order was passed on 28.07.1973 transferring the land in question to the Municipal Corporation, Indore.
5. Subsequently, on 14.04.1976, the then Commissioner, Indore Division, directed the SDO to assess the compensation.

In this regard, writ petition for NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:21289 2 CONC-2760-2024 acquisition was filed in the year 2023 and an order dated 08.01.2024 was passed directing the Land Acquisition Officer to pass an appropriate order.

6. It has further been stated that the Act of 1956 was repealed in the year 1976, and a new Act,
namely the Gandi Basti Kshetra (Sudhar Tatha Nirmulan) Adhiniyam, 1976, came into effect, in which there is no saving clause for the 1956 Act.

entities.text: Gandi Basti Kshetra (Sudhar Tatha Nirmulan) Adhiniyam, 1976
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 7. As such, it was concluded that no order with respect to the acquisition under the Act, 1956 can now be passed.
The petitioner has attempted to challenge the correctness of this order in the present contempt petition.
8. This Court is of the view that the correctness of the order cannot be examined in a contempt petition.
In the opinion of this Court, the order passed by the Writ Court has been complied with.
If the petitioner is not satisfied with the same, he is at liberty to assail the said order by instituting appropriate proceedings.
9. Accordingly, the present contempt petition is disposed of.
Notices issued to the respondents are hereby discharged and the petitioner is granted liberty to challenge the order 24.12.2025.
